column1: # More German learner notes, written by Claude (origin "claude"), applied by notes.py: entry id|typical learner mistake|usage note
de:doch:particle||As an answer, doch means "yes" after a negative question: "Kommst du nicht?" "Doch!" (Yes, I am coming). In a request it softens or urges: "Komm doch mit!"
de:mal:particle||Mal makes a request softer and friendlier: "Kannst du mal kommen?", "Schau mal!"
de:halt:adverb||Halt (in Switzerland and the south also "eben") means "that's just how it is": "Das ist halt so."
de:noch:adverb|"Noch nicht" means not yet, "nicht mehr" means no longer; "noch ein Bier" means another beer.|
de:dürfen:verb|"Du darfst nicht" means you must not (it is forbidden).|Dürfen asks for permission: "Darf ich hier rauchen?"
de:müssen:verb|"Du musst nicht" means you don't have to, not "you must not" (that is "du darfst nicht").|
de:sollen:verb||Sollen is what someone else wants or expects: "Ich soll morgen anrufen" (I'm supposed to call tomorrow).
de:brauchen:verb|"Du brauchst nicht zu kommen" means you don't need to come (brauchen + zu, usually with nicht or nur).|
de:lassen:verb||Lassen means to let and also to have something done: "Ich lasse mein Velo reparieren" (I'm having my bike repaired).
de:kennenlernen:verb|To meet someone for the first time is kennenlernen, not treffen: "Ich habe sie in Zürich kennengelernt".|
de:schmecken:verb||"Es schmeckt mir" means I like the taste. "Schmeckt's?" is asked at the table.
de:aufhören:verb|"Aufhören mit" + noun, or "aufhören zu" + infinitive: "Hör auf zu rauchen!"|
de:besuchen:verb|Besuchen takes no preposition: "Ich besuche meine Oma". With a place it also means to attend: "eine Schule besuchen".|
de:Frau:noun||Frau means woman, wife and Mrs (Frau Müller). "Meine Frau" is my wife.
de:Herr:noun||Herr means Mr (Herr Meier) and gentleman. Its other forms take -n: "Ich spreche mit Herrn Meier".
de:Kind:noun|"Das Kind" is neuter, also for a girl or boy: "das Kind, es".|
de:weg:adverb|Weg (away, gone) is different from "der Weg" (the way, the path): "Mein Velo ist weg!"|
de:sicher:adjective||Sicher means safe and sure: "Hier bist du sicher" (safe), "Bist du sicher?" (sure).
de:dann:adverb|"Dann" means then (after that); "denn" means because, or adds interest to a question ("Was ist denn los?").|
de:wo:adverb|Wo asks where something is; wohin asks where to, woher where from: "Wohin gehst du?"|
de:ihr:pronoun||Ihr is the plural "you" (ihr seid), and also "her" (ich gebe ihr) and "her/their" (ihr Buch). Ihr with a capital I is the polite "your".
de:sich:pronoun|Many everyday verbs need sich: "sich freuen", "sich setzen", "sich erinnern". "Ich setze mich", not "ich setze".|
de:gleich:adverb||Gleich means right away, soon ("Ich komme gleich") and also the same ("das gleiche Buch").
de:Angst:noun|"Angst haben vor" + dative: "Ich habe Angst vor Hunden".|
de:Hunger:noun|"Ich habe Hunger" (I have hunger), not "ich bin hungrig" in everyday speech; the same with Durst.|
de:ziemlich:adverb||Ziemlich means quite, rather: "ziemlich gut".
de:damals:adverb|"Damals" is back then (a past period); "dann" is then (next).|
de:schaffen:verb||Schaffen meaning "to manage" is weak: schaffte, geschafft ("Ich habe es geschafft!"). Meaning "to create" it is strong: schuf, geschaffen.
de:hängen:verb||Hängen with an object is weak: "Ich habe das Bild an die Wand gehängt." Without one it is strong: "Das Bild hing / hat (CH: ist) an der Wand gehangen."
de:überlegen:verb||"Sich etwas überlegen" means to think something over: "Ich überlege es mir."
